overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop on move two and keeps the c-pawn flexible, aiming for a Catalan, Réti or King's Indian Fianchetto set-up depending on Black's reply. Black usually chooses 2...g6 or 2...c5, with 2...e5 (Ueberlinger Gambit) as a rare try. The game is typically a slow positional fight around the long diagonal and the centre.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, Nf3, O-O and c4, transposing to a Catalan or Fianchetto KID.
Pressure along the long diagonal and decide on c4 or c3 later.

black_ideas.idea: 2...g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 for a King's Indian Fianchetto with ...d6 and ...e5.
2...c5 3.d5 b5 for a Benko-style counterplay, or ...e6 and ...d5 for a Catalan-like game.

typical_structures.structure: Fianchetto structures with a flexible centre: d4 with c4 or c3 and Bg2 against Black's fianchetto or ...d5 set-up.

character.notes: Positional manoeuvring with long-diagonal bishops; not forcing.

gambit.notes: No material offered; 2...e5 is Black's gambit sideline.

soundness.notes: Fully sound, a quiet and respectable second move.

structure.notes: Centre stays flexible with c-pawn and e-pawn choices left open.

approach.notes: Played by strong players as part of Catalan-type play, standard rather than a universal system.

level.notes: Plans matter more than theory; fianchetto play is easy to follow.

sublines_that_differ.name: Ueberlinger Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a pawn for activity; unclear and rare.

character.reason: Quiet positional play that is neither especially hard to crack nor forcing.

gambit.reason: No material offered in the main line.

structure.reason: Fianchetto set-up leaves the centre undecided.

approach.reason: Close to Catalan systems but White's moves vary by Black's reply.

level.reason: Plans of the Catalan type are not trivial but there is little theory.

plans.reason: Long-diagonal bishop and pressure on the Black centre.
